title: ‘It’s Like a Movie’: LISA Talks ‘PRESS PLAY’ on ‘The Tonight Show’

summary: Can't follow or block anyone on Spotify right now? You’re not alone.
body: Credit: Rita El Khoury / Android Authority TL;DR Spotify users are reporting that they are unable to follow/unfollow other accounts. Users are also getting an error message when trying to block/unblock other users. Spotify says it is aware of the issue, but can’t provide a timeframe for when it will be addressed. Spotify is in the middle of rolling out a new toggle that will save parents’ personal recommendations from getting contaminated by kids’ music. Coincidentally, it looks like a separate feature broke right after this toggle was announced. What’s worse is that it may take a while before this feature is fixed. Spotify users are reporting that they are unable to follow and unfollow other accounts on the platform. As one user describes the situation, when they tap the follow button, the button state changes to “Following,” as it should. However, the follower count does not change and when the page is refreshed, the button reverts to “Follow.”

title: Is Phone 4b secretly a CMF device? Carl Pei addresses rebranding rumors
summary: Nothing CEO sets the record straight, confirming it's a direct successor to the Phone 3a Lite instead.
body: Credit: Nothing / YouTube TL;DR Nothing CEO Carl Pei is denying theories that the Phone 4b was a repurposed CMF Phone 3 Pro, instead confirming it is the direct successor to the Phone 3a Lite. Nothing dropped the “a Lite” moniker in favor of the simpler “b” tag to keep product tiers easy to digest amid rising memory costs. Despite community controversy over its placement and design, early Phone 4b sales are tracking at roughly double the company’s internal targets. The launch of the Nothing Phone 4b raised plenty of eyebrows across the tech community, with many questioning where the new budget device actually fits in the company’s portfolio. While Nothing’s leadership previously stepped in to clarify the Phone 4b’s branding and identity , Nothing CEO Carl Pei has now directly responded to community theories claiming the Phone 4b was originally conceived as a rebranded CMF phone. In a reaction video on the company’s official YouTube channel (also highlighted more recently in a YouTube Short ), Pei flatly dismissed the idea that the Phone 4b was a repurposed product from Nothing’s budget-centric CMF sub-brand.

title: Apple claims the iPhone 18 Pro camera is more secure than your Android
summary: It says photo verification systems on Android devices are less secure and private.
body: TL;DR Apple launched “Reference Image,” a new verified photography mode, with the iPhone 18 Pro series. The company claims its implementation is more secure than C2PA-based systems used in Android phones. Reference Image signs pictures at the sensor level, whereas C2PA signs images after they are processed. Google introduced verified photography with the Pixel 10 series using the C2PA standard and also brought it to the Pixel 11 range . Apple, by contrast, only started offering support for verified photography with the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max — an entire generation after the Pixel 10 series. However, the company now claims its “Reference Image” is much better than the C2PA standard used by companies like Google and Samsung. In a new blog post , Apple shared extensive insights into how Reference Image works and why it’s better than anything else available to the general public. Reference Image is an opt-in feature that works on the primary camera of the iPhone 18 Pro series. It adds a cryptographic signature to the photo the moment the sensor captures it, before any image processing. The rollout lands just ahead of the Googlebook launch, pushing Google’s broader cross-device vision closer to reality. Googlebooks aren’t going to be laptops meant to exist on their own, and the more interesting part promises to be what happens when you put one next to your Android phone. Google has spent months laying that groundwork, from Android 17’s Continue On task handoff to Play Services’ hooks for Googlebook setup and experiments that could turn your phone into a laptop trackpad .
